text: A good name is worth more than great riches; to be held in esteem is better than silver or gold.
Rich and poor meet together; the LORD is the maker of them all.
The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple walk on and pay the price.
Humility and the fear of the LORD bring their reward: riches and honor and life.

versions.text: The reward of humility and the fear of the LORD is riches and honor and life.
versions.explanation: The compound subject ("the reward of humility and the fear of the LORD") followed by singular "is" reads awkwardly and slows oral delivery. Recasting the line keeps the sense while giving a cleaner rhythm.

text: Thorns and snares lie in the path of the crooked; whoever guards his life stays far from them.
Train a child in the way he should go, and even when he is old he will not turn from it.
The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.
Whoever sows injustice reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.

versions.text: Whoever sows injustice reaps trouble, and the rod of his fury will fail.
versions.explanation: יִכְלֶה means to be finished off, consumed, or destroyed. "Fail" is vague in English and loses the sense of the oppressor's instrument of anger being brought to nothing.

text: The generous will be blessed, for they share their bread with the poor.
Drive out the mocker, and strife goes with him; quarrels and insults come to an end.
Whoever loves a pure heart and speaks with grace will have the king as a friend.
The eyes of the LORD watch over knowledge, but he overturns the words of the treacherous.
The sluggard says, "There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!"
The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; the one the LORD is angry with falls into it.
Folly is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far from him.
Whoever oppresses the poor to enrich himself, or gives to the rich, will come to poverty.
Turn your ear and listen to the words of the wise; set your heart on what I teach.
It is pleasant to keep them within you, to have them all ready on your lips.
So that your trust may be in the LORD, I am teaching you today—yes, you.
Have I not written for you thirty sayings of counsel and knowledge,
to teach you true and reliable words, so that you may give a sound answer to those who send you?
Do not rob the poor because they are poor, and do not crush the afflicted in court,
for the LORD will take up their case and will rob of life those who rob them.

versions.text: for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who plunder them.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew ends with נָפֶשׁ ("life/soul"), which is the object of the LORD's action: he despoils the despoilers of their very life. The current rendering drops this element, weakening the force of the threat.

text: Do not make friends with a hot-tempered man, and do not keep company with anyone given to rage,
or you may learn his ways and bring a snare upon your own soul.

versions.text: or you may learn his ways and set a snare for your own soul.
versions.explanation: "Set a snare for" normally implies trapping someone else; the Hebrew idiom (לָקַחְתָּ מוֹקֵשׁ לְנַפְשֶׁךָ) means taking/bringing a trap upon oneself. "Bring a snare upon" conveys the self-inflicted danger more clearly.

text: Do not be one who strikes hands in pledge or puts up security for debts;
if you have nothing to pay with, why should your very bed be taken from under you?
Do not move the ancient boundary stone set up by your fathers.
Do you see someone skilled in his work? He will stand before kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
